figures.name: Asalluhi
figures.description: Eridu's god of incantation and exorcism, son of Enki; later identified with Marduk as the great magician among the gods.

figures.name: Atrahasis
figures.description: The 'exceedingly wise' king of Shuruppak whom Enki warned of the coming Flood; hero of the Atrahasis epic, remembered in later tradition as Ziusudra and as Utnapishtim.

figures.name: Bau
figures.description: Goddess of healing and of the city of Lagash, consort of Ningirsu (Ninurta) and daughter of An; her animal symbol was the dog.

figures.name: Birtum
figures.description: God of the underworld, consort of the prison goddess Nungal.

figures.name: Ennanatum I
figures.description: Ruler (ensi) of Lagash of the First Dynasty of Lagash; son of Akurgal, brother of Eannatum and father of Entemena.

figures.name: Haya
figures.description: God of grain stores and husband of the scribal goddess Nisaba; patron of scribes and stewards, and in some traditions father of Ninlil.

figures.name: Meshka
figures.description: Figure recorded from a name-list source; almost nothing is known beyond the name.

figures.name: Muati
figures.description: Old Babylonian god regarded as the spouse of Nanaya; later equated with Nabu, whose name Muati effectively became in the first millennium BCE.

figures.name: Mār-bīti
figures.description: Babylonian deity whose name means 'son of the temple'; chief god of the city of Der.

figures.name: Nindub
figures.description: Minor deity attested in the An = Anum god list; little beyond the name is preserved.

figures.name: Nineigara
figures.description: Minor deity attested in Mesopotamian god lists; surviving references are sparse.

figures.name: Ningishzida
figures.description: The 'lord of the good tree', god of vegetation, snakes and the underworld; son of Ninazu, whose emblem was the horned serpent-dragon.

figures.name: Ninirigal
figures.description: Minor deity attested in the An = Anum god list.

figures.name: Ninkarnunna
figures.description: Minor deity attested in Mesopotamian god lists; details are sparse.

figures.name: Ninmeurur
figures.description: Minor deity attested in the An = Anum god list.

figures.name: Nisaba
figures.description: Goddess of grain and of writing and accounting; wife of Haya and patroness of scribes.

figures.name: Sutītu
figures.description: Deified form of the Sutean nomads, attested in god lists and personal names.

figures.name: Ukulla
figures.description: Minor deity attested in Mesopotamian god lists.

figures.name: Urnunta-ea
figures.description: Minor deity attested in Mesopotamian god lists; the name joins 'Urnunta' with the god Ea.

figures.name: Zagar
figures.description: God of dreams, attendant of the moon god Nanna/Sin, who carried dream messages to humankind.
